exposure: Vaginal delivery after obstetric anal sphincter injury
Elective cesarean delivery after obstetric anal sphincter injury
outcome: Quality of life affected by anal incontinence
cohort: 1978 women with a history of obstetric anal sphincter injury at first delivery and a subsequent second delivery
finding: While women with a second vaginal delivery had a higher risk of worsening anal incontinence symptoms compared to those with an elective cesarean delivery, the mode of second delivery did not significantly affect the long-term risk of anal or fecal incontinence after adjusting for maternal and obstetric characteristics.
mod_finding: Mode of second delivery (vaginal vs. elective cesarean) did not significantly affect the risk of long-term anal or fecal incontinence in multivariable analyses, although there was a trend towards lower risk in the elective cesarean group.
